message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is generally referred to as a **multinucleated** cell. In biology we often call such a structure a **syncytium** (or **polykaryon**) when it results from fusion of individual cells. Classic examples include:

| Cell type | Typical function | Example of multinucleation |
|-----------|------------------|----------------------------|
| Skeletal muscle fiber | Contractile tissue | Myofiber (muscle fiber) |
| Osteoclast | Bone resorption | Giant osteoclast |
| Placental syncytiotrophoblast | Nutrient exchange between mother and fetus | Syncytiotrophoblast layer |
| Certain fungal hyphae | Growth and nutrient transport | Hyphal network |

So if you’re looking for a general term, “multinucleated” or “syncytium” is what you’d use.
